There are also specific risks or events that could push outcomes outside the stated confidence intervals. For example, any major geopolitical events, dramatic policy changes, or sudden shocks—like natural disasters, market crashes, or unforeseen technological breakthroughs—could generate outcomes well beyond the projected range. These events tend to have low probabilities but high impacts when they occur. Additionally, if there are factors that weren’t fully captured in the model, such as abrupt changes in sentiment or data inaccuracies, they could skew results beyond the anticipated range. While these risks are difficult to predict precisely, their possibility can never be fully ruled out.
